artists.biography: Belinda Jo Carlisle (born August 17, 1958) is an American singer who gained worldwide fame as the lead vocalist of the Go-Go's, one of the most successful all-female bands of all time and the first such group whose members wrote their own songs and played their own instruments. Topping the Billboard charts with the Go-Go's, she sold more than seven million albums in just three years and later went on to a successful solo career with hits "Mad About You", "Summer Rain", "I Get Weak", "Circle in the Sand", "Leave a Light On" and "Heaven Is a Place on Earth" among others, which were major successes in the United States and United Kingdom as well as internationally. Her autobiography, Lips Unsealed, published in June 2010, reached No. 27 on the The New York Times Best Seller list and received favorable reviews. On August 11, 2011, she received, as a member of the Go-Go's, a star on the Hollywood Walk of Fame.

perplexity.description:
Belinda is the debut solo album by American singer Belinda Carlisle, released on May 19, 1986, by I.R.S. Records. Following the breakup of her band The Go-Go's, Carlisle embarked on a solo career with this album, which blends rock with melodic pop influences. The record features a polished 1980s rock sound with catchy hooks, highlighted by the lead single "Mad About You," which reached number 3 on the US Billboard Hot 100 and topped the Canadian charts. The album also includes a cover of Freda Payne's "Band of Gold," which was remixed for single release with backing vocals by Payne herself.

Musically, Belinda showcases Carlisle's transition from the punk-influenced style of The Go-Go's to a more mainstream rock and pop approach, setting the foundation for her later commercial success. The album was certified gold in the United States and platinum in Canada, marking a strong start to her solo career. While it did not reach the same level of international chart dominance as her follow-up album Heaven on Earth (1987), Belinda established her as a credible solo artist and helped define her musical identity in the mid-1980s rock scene.
